summary: Polymorphism means one method call, like student.report(), runs the version that belongs to the object's actual class. You can loop over mixed objects and treat them the same way.
notes: HonorsStudent overrides report() with the same name and parameters as Student.report().
The for loop never checks the type. Python looks up report() on each object when the line runs.
roster[0].weighted_average() raises AttributeError only when that line runs, not before.
pitfall: Spelling an override differently, like def reprt(self), does not override anything. The loop quietly calls the parent's report() instead.
